SEPTEMBER 26

Don't worry about the censor. He doesn't cut out anything important. All officers' mail is theoretically censored at the base censor's office or main post office. They pay particular attention to new outfits and those that are moving - others are not censored so closely. Hence many letters are not opened by them and many are, depending on the outfit. They keep their eyes on an outfit like this though, and as I have said before, a division is handled and handles itself entirely differently from a Service of Supply unit, a battalion or any separate unit. They get away with many things that a division cannot, and they likewise cannot do many things which we can.

Had another nice little jaunt today and saw more of this part of the country. Almost froze to death before returning but enjoyed the trip and got a few more supplies. The bicycles here are amazing and the riders even more so. Did I tell you about seeing a family the other day? A young boy about eleven headed the parade, followed by mother and dad on a tandem, with the baby in a side car. Young sister came pedaling up behind on small] bike. Everybody rides. They must put them on bikes as soon as they can walk.

The country roads are really beautiful and the whole place is like a toy land. Narrow roads and Bantam cars - our “peeps” (you probably call them "jeeps" look like a truck compared to them. The pubs are as near to a town hall meeting as any place I have been. Never crowded (not much anyway) although many army men are usually found there. The men gather in the pubs at noon and in the early evening and some in the tea shops in the middle of the morning or afternoon. Women seldom go to the pubs, except the younger ones, but they have tea.

One thing I can't get used to is their women smoking. Golly, they say the Americans smoke a lot, but we never see many women smoking on the street. They peddle madly down the road on their bikes with a cigarette sticking out exactly in the middle of their lips. They scrub windows and shop, they walk on the streets and wait in their lines -

What could be more beautiful than a day in June - or October? That is one thing we have had the breaks on so far - the weather. And the days of our movements have been funny too. We may not go to church very often, but we sure work on Sundays! We left the “old country” on a Sunday and
now again on a Sunday we are on the water headed I cannot] say where, although it is more or less obvious.
